simple.meaning: יָרִיב (yârîyb) is a Hebrew word meaning “literally he will contend ; properly, adjective contentious ; used as noun, an adversary.” BibleIQ connects the English word back to this source word so its use can be compared across Scripture.
simple.biblicalBackground: יָרִיב (H3401) appears 3 times in the Hebrew Bible, beginning at Psalms 35:1, with occurrences in Psalms, Isaiah, Jeremiah.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to יָרִיב (H3401) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: English translations can use the same English word for different Hebrew words. BibleIQ anchors the study in יָרִיב (H3401) before moving outward to related references.
simple.summary: יָרִיב (yârîyb) / H3401 is traced through Psalms 35:1, Isaiah 49:25, Jeremiah 18:19 using source-language evidence and occurrence comparison.

definitions.short: literally he will contend ; properly, adjective contentious ; used as noun, an adversary
definitions.full: H3401. yarib I. [ יָרִיב ] noun [masculine] opponent, adversary (Ges § 85d ); — suffix (of Zion), יְדִיבֵךְ Isa 49:26 ( רִיבֵךְ ᵐ5 so Du); compare plural suffix יְרִיבַ֑י Psa 35:1 (|| לֹחֲמָ֑י ); of personal opponent, יְרִיבָ֑י Jer 18:19 ( דִיבִי ᵐ5 , so Gie).
